query: For as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys in the form of nanoscale thin films or lithographically patterned nanoribbons, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their magnetocaloric response and hysteresis during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles, given that the notable response reported for bulk forms may not persist in a genuinely low-dimensional state and that heat-transfer rate limits cycle frequency? Specify one controlled intervention, predicted observations relative to the as-deposited baseline, applicable operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: In nanoscale (≤150 nm) as-deposited Fe–Mn–Ni–Ge–Si high-entropy alloy (HEA) films, compressive in-plane growth stress and chemical disorder jointly suppress the sharp magneto-structural transition that underlies the bulk magnetocaloric effect (MCE), broadening the hysteresis loop and cutting the isothermal entropy change (ΔS_M). A brief sub-eutectic rapid-thermal anneal (400 °C, 120 s, vacuum) that relaxes the residual stress and promotes incipient B2-type chemical ordering will restore cooperative lattice distortion, thereby doubling ΔS_M and shrinking thermal hysteresis by >50 % under a low applied field (0.3 T) at 300 K.
generation.material_initial_state: As-deposited, non-equiatomic FeₓMnᵧNi_zGe_uSi_v high-entropy alloy sputtered onto a 200 nm SiO₂/Si wafer: 100 nm thick, nanocrystalline (grain size ≈8 nm), strong in-plane compressive stress (~0.8 GPa), chemically disordered bcc solid solution, no post-deposition heat treatment.
generation.intervention: Single rapid-thermal-anneal (RTA) at 400 °C for 120 s in high vacuum (≤10⁻⁵ mbar), followed by fast quench to room temperature while kept on the substrate.
generation.conditions: Magnetocaloric cycling between 280 K and 320 K in an out-of-plane magnetic field μ₀H ≤0.3 T; cycle period 1 s (≤10 Hz heat-transfer-limited operation).
generation.structural_mediator: Partial relief of in-plane compressive stress (to ≤0.2 GPa) and emergence of short-range B2 ordering within grains (correlation length 2–3 nm) without significant grain growth.
generation.mechanism: Stress relaxation lowers the elastic energy penalty for the first-order martensitic-like transition, while B2 ordering raises the magneto-structural coupling coefficient. Together they sharpen the transition, enhancing the entropy change per unit field and reducing nucleation barriers, which narrows hysteresis.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with the as-deposited baseline, RTA-treated films will exhibit: 1) Peak |ΔS_M| increased from ~2 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ to ≥4 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ at μ₀ΔH = 0.3 T and 300 K; 2) Thermal hysteresis width (ΔT_hyst) reduced from ~5 K to ≤2 K; 3) Magnetic-cooling cycle frequency limited by heat extraction rising from ~3 Hz to ≥10 Hz because of reduced latent-heat load per cycle and slightly higher thermal conductivity (≈+15 %).
generation.baseline: As-deposited film tested under identical field and temperature sweep shows |ΔS_M| ≈2 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and ΔT_hyst ≈5 K, with functional MCE only up to ~3 Hz due to heat-transfer limits.
generation.boundary: Effect expected only for films 30–150 nm thick on substrates having thermal expansion mismatch ≤0.2 %. RTA temperatures >500 °C or dwell times >5 min that coarsen grains (>20 nm) or fully order the lattice will re-widen hysteresis and diminish ΔS_M. Nanoribbons narrower than ~200 nm may fracture during RTA, invalidating the hypothesis.
generation.uncertainty: No direct prior data on nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi HEA MCE exists; magnitude of stress relaxation and degree of B2 ordering achievable without grain growth are uncertain, so the predicted doubling of ΔS_M may vary by ±0.5 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare three identical 100 nm FeMnNiGeSi films (A, B, C) on SiO₂/Si. Keep A as-deposited. Subject B and C to RTA at 400 °C for 120 s; additionally anneal C at 550 °C for 5 min to induce grain growth. Measure residual stress (wafer curvature), XRD for B2 ordering (superlattice peaks), grain size (TEM), and time-resolved M(H,T) loops during 1 s cycles.
measurements: ΔS_M (J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) at μ₀ΔH=0.3 T
Sustainable cycle frequency at 90 % of ΔS_M
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If film B does NOT show (i) ≥40 % reduction in residual stress, (ii) detectable increase in B2 ordering, AND (iii) either |ΔS_M| increase <10 % OR hysteresis reduction <10 % relative to film A under identical test conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
